events.text: Analyst request: several cards this month show purchases from the same unusual device profile. Review transaction 3478561 on card C13487-K1 and look for related activity.

events.msg: Core toolkit: flagged transaction, card window, card baseline, recurring charges, resolved account history, device neighbours, region activity and prior cases

hypotheses: Account Takeover (ATO) by a fraud ring using a shared, fully specified device profile and anonymous proxies to cash out compromised cards
Legitimate transaction where the cardholder is using a new mobile device and a VPN/proxy for privacy

calls.why: To identify the other 19 cards and customers sharing this specific device profile, and to check if any of those accounts have confirmed fraud cases.
To review the recent history of card C13487-K1 for other unusual online transactions or signs of compromise.

events.msg: Four specialist analysts reviewing their evidence in parallel

events.assessment: Transaction 3478561 on card C13487-K1 represents a high-risk event. The cardholder's baseline consists almost entirely of in-person transactions (69 out of 71), whereas this transaction is online, uses an anonymous proxy, and is associated with a specific, non-generic device profile ('SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080') that has been linked to 114 transactions across the system.
key_points: Transaction 3478561 is a significant departure from the cardholder's historical baseline, which is 97% in-person 'W' product transactions.
The transaction was conducted via an anonymous proxy ('IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS') and flagged as a 'New' device for this card.
The specific device profile used is highly active across the network, appearing in 114 transactions, indicating a shared fraudulent device or botnet rather than a single user's device.

events.assessment: The transaction on card C13487-K1 was conducted using a fully specified, new mobile device profile associated with an anonymous proxy. Since this card has only one recorded transaction, the combination of a new device and proxy usage indicates a high risk of fraud. Further investigation is needed to confirm if this device has been used across other accounts as suggested by the alert.
key_points: The transaction on card C13487-K1 was performed using a fully specified device profile (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080) flagged as 'New'.
The connection utilized an anonymous proxy ('IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS'), which is a common indicator of obfuscation.
The card account C13487-K1 has a history of only 1 transaction, occurring on 2016-11-22, meaning there is no established trusted behavior for this card.

events.assessment: Transaction 3478561 on card C13487-K1 is part of a larger cluster of transactions sharing the same device profile, with 52 cards associated all-time. All observed transactions in this group utilize anonymous proxies (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS) and are flagged as 'New' devices, suggesting a coordinated card-not-present campaign rather than isolated organic behavior.
key_points: Card C13487-K1 initiated transaction 3460634 on 2016-11-15 using an anonymous proxy, which shares the same device profile as 51 other cards.
Multiple distinct cards, including C10326-K1, C01996-K2, and C09906-K1, show a pattern of sequential 'New' device transactions utilizing anonymous proxies within a short timeframe.
The transaction model scores for these transactions remain low-to-moderate (ranging from 0.01 to 0.28), which may indicate the pattern is successfully bypassing standard real-time risk thresholds.

events.assessment: The alert regarding transaction 3478561 on card C13487-K1 is highly suspicious due to its association with a recurring fraudulent device profile. Multiple closed cases (CC-2985, CC-2971, CC-3035, and CC-2649) confirm a pattern of unauthorized online purchases originating from a Samsung SM-G935F on Chrome for Android behind an anonymous proxy. This indicates a coordinated card-not-present fraud campaign using a shared, specific device signature across unrelated cardholders.
key_points: Four closed cases (CC-2985, CC-2971, CC-3035, and CC-2649) were confirmed as fraud involving the exact same Samsung SM-G935F device profile behind an anonymous proxy.
The fraudulent activity across these closed cases involved multiple unrelated cardholders (C06617, C09998, C09733, and C03528) reporting unauthorized online purchases.
Similar historical cases like CC-0334 and CC-5122 also confirm unauthorized card-not-present transactions using variants of the SM-G935F device profile.

events.claim: The transaction model trained on the bank's own closed cases (4,665 confirmed-fraud and 900 cleared investigations, July-October; October hold-out AUC 0.973) scores this transaction 0.064, against a 2.1% base rate. It reads the unnamed Vesta C/D/M/V columns, the identity record, running aggregates of the resolved account and the graph's memory of earlier closed cases, all as known at transaction time (it never sees the case outcome)
The session was routed through an anonymous proxy

The same device profile (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080) was used on 19 other card(s) of 19 other customer(s) between 2016-11-14 and 2016-11-22, 24 of those uses as a New device, 24 behind an anonymising proxy. events.what_would_change_verdict: The verdict is solid based on the rare, fully specified device profile used as a New device by 19 other customers behind an anonymizing proxy, which is strong evidence of a coordinated ring. If the device profile were generic (e.g., missing model/OS/screen fields) or if the other cards belonged to the same customer, the probability would be significantly lower and the verdict might change.
